routes.label: Convert the area before applying the density

question: A rectangular field is \(300\) feet wide and \(400\) feet long. Random sampling indicates that there are, on the average, three ants per square inch throughout the field. [\(12\) inches = \(1\) foot.] Of the following, the number that most closely approximates the number of ants in the field is
solution:
The density is given per square inch, so we need the field's area in square inches. A square measuring one foot on each side measures \(12\) inches on each side, so
\[
1\text{ square foot}=12\cdot12=144\text{ square inches}.
\]
The rectangular field has area
\[
300\cdot400=120{,}000\text{ square feet}.
\]
Applying the sampled average of three ants per square inch gives the estimate
\[
120{,}000\cdot144\cdot3=51{,}840{,}000
\]
ants, or \(51.84\) million ants. This is only \(1.84\) million from \(50\) million. Every other choice is at most \(5\) million or at least \(500\) million, so each is farther away. The best approximation is \(\boxed{50\text{ million}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
